answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small, time-locked copper-backed bond before it can transact. Honest agents earn the bond back through verified work, while a fake identity that misbehaves loses it, so creating thousands of throwaway agents becomes expensive. Reputation then acts as a bridge between past behaviour and future trust: agents with a proven history climb toward a summit of higher limits, while newcomers stay capped until they prove themselves.
